meta.name: SELinux Testcases - Android + Linux
notes: Run these commands on the target shell. For Android, typically prefix with: adb shell '<command>'.
Checks are designed to minimize false positives: only a few are strict pass/fail; most are evidence collectors.
Some evidence checks may require root (noted per check).

checks.label: SELinux mode is Enforcing (authoritative)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v getenforce >/dev/null 2>&1; then getenforce 2>/dev/null; elif [ -r /sys/fs/selinux/enforce ]; then v=$(cat /sys/fs/selinux/enforce 2>/dev/null); [ "$v" = "1" ] && echo Enforcing || echo Permissive; else echo Permissive; fi'
checks.description: Fail if SELinux is not enforcing. getenforce explicitly reports enforcing/permissive/disabled.
checks.remediation: Run 'setenforce 1' to switch to enforcing mode. Set SELINUX=enforcing in /etc/selinux/config for persistence.

checks.label: Kernel cmdline does not disable SELinux
checks.command: sh -c 'if [ -r /proc/cmdline ] && grep -Eq "(androidboot\.selinux=permissive|selinux=0|enforcing=0)" /proc/cmdline 2>/dev/null; then echo BAD; else echo OK; fi'
checks.description: Fails only if explicit disable/permissive flags are present in /proc/cmdline.
checks.remediation: Remove selinux=0, enforcing=0, or androidboot.selinux=permissive from the kernel command line or bootloader config.

checks.label: SELinux enable file exists and shows enforcing bit (1)
checks.command: sh -c 'if [ -r /sys/fs/selinux/enforce ]; then cat /sys/fs/selinux/enforce 2>/dev/null; else echo NO_FILE; fi'
checks.description: Checks /sys/fs/selinux/enforce (1=enforcing, 0=permissive). Missing file suggests SELinux not mounted/enabled.
checks.remediation: Run 'echo 1 > /sys/fs/selinux/enforce' as root. If the file is missing, ensure SELinux is installed and selinuxfs is mounted.

checks.label: SELinux policy is present (policy node exists)
checks.command: sh -c 'if [ -e /sys/fs/selinux/policy ] || [ -e /sys/fs/selinux/enforce ] || command -v getenforce >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo PRESENT; else echo MISSING; fi'
checks.description: Verifies that a policy blob is loaded (non-empty policy file).
checks.remediation: Install the SELinux policy package (e.g., selinux-policy-targeted) and reboot to load the policy.

checks.label: selinuxenabled utility reports enabled (if available)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1; then selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && echo ENABLED || echo DISABLED; else echo NO_TOOL; fi'
checks.description: If selinuxenabled exists, it exits 0 when enabled. If missing, it does not fail.
checks.remediation: Install SELinux utilities (policycoreutils) and enable SELinux in /etc/selinux/config, then reboot.

checks.label: sestatus reports enabled + enforcing (if available)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v sestatus >/dev/null 2>&1; then (sestatus 2>/dev/null | grep -qi "SELinux status: *enabled" && sestatus 2>/dev/null | grep -qi "Current mode: *enforcing") && echo ENFORCING || echo NOT_ENFORCING; else echo NO_TOOL; fi'
checks.description: Uses sestatus when present to confirm enabled+enforcing. If sestatus is missing, it does not fail.
checks.remediation: Set SELINUX=enforcing in /etc/selinux/config and run 'setenforce 1'. Reboot if SELinux was fully disabled.

checks.label: Linux config requests enforcing (if config file exists)
checks.command: sh -c 'if [ -r /etc/selinux/config ]; then v=$(grep -E "^[[:space:]]*SELINUX=" /etc/selinux/config | tail -n 1 | tr -d "\r" ); echo "$v"; else echo NO_FILE; fi'
checks.description: If /etc/selinux/config exists, flags permissive/disabled. Missing file does not fail.
checks.remediation: Edit /etc/selinux/config and change SELINUX=permissive or SELINUX=disabled to SELINUX=enforcing.

checks.label: selinuxfs appears mounted
checks.command: sh -c 'grep -Eq "\bselinuxfs\b" /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null && echo MOUNTED || echo NOT_MOUNTED'
checks.description: If SELinux is active, selinuxfs is typically mounted.
checks.remediation: Mount selinuxfs with 'mount -t selinuxfs selinuxfs /sys/fs/selinux'. Ensure SELinux is enabled in the kernel config.

checks.label: Current shell has an SELinux context (id -Z)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v id >/dev/null 2>&1; then id -Z 2>/dev/null || echo NO_CONTEXT; else echo NO_ID; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: prints SELinux context for current identity.
checks.remediation: If no context is shown, ensure SELinux is enabled and the 'id' command supports the -Z flag.

checks.label: Process contexts available (ps -eZ)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1; then ps -eZ 2>/dev/null | head -n 15; else echo NO_PS; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: lists processes with contexts (first 15 lines).
checks.remediation: If contexts are missing, verify SELinux is enforcing and procps supports -Z. Relabel the filesystem if needed.

checks.label: setenforce present (and not blocked)
checks.command: sh -c 'command -v setenforce >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo PRESENT || echo MISSING'
checks.description: Evidence: confirms setenforce tool availability (does not change mode).
checks.remediation: Install the policycoreutils package to get setenforce and other SELinux management tools.

checks.label: getsebool available (Linux SELinux booleans)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v getsebool >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo PRESENT; getsebool -a 2>/dev/null | head -n 20; else echo MISSING; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: booleans exist and are readable (first 20 lines).
checks.remediation: Install policycoreutils and selinux-policy-targeted to get getsebool and SELinux boolean support.

checks.label: semodule list available (installed policy modules)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v semodule >/dev/null 2>&1; then semodule -l 2>/dev/null | head -n 30; else echo NO_SEMODULE; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: shows loaded SELinux modules (first 30 lines).
checks.remediation: Install policycoreutils-python-utils for semodule. Run 'semodule -l' as root to list policy modules.

checks.label: Android: count SELinux denials in logcat (avc:)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v logcat >/dev/null 2>&1; then c=$(logcat -b all -T 1000 -d 2>/dev/null | grep -ci "avc:"); echo "AVC_LOGCAT_COUNT=$c"; else echo NO_LOGCAT; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: counts 'avc:' denials in logcat.
checks.remediation: Review AVC denials with 'logcat -b all | grep avc' and update SELinux policy to resolve legitimate access needs.

checks.label: Android: count SELinux denials in dmesg (avc:)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v dmesg >/dev/null 2>&1; then c=$(dmesg 2>/dev/null | grep -ci "avc:"); echo "AVC_DMESG_COUNT=$c"; else echo NO_DMESG; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: counts 'avc:' denials in dmesg.
checks.remediation: Review AVC denials with 'dmesg | grep avc' and update SELinux policy or fix mislabeled files as needed.

checks.label: Android: previous-boot denials via pstore console-ramoops (if present)
checks.command: sh -c 'ls /sys/fs/pstore/console-ramoops* >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo NO_PSTORE; exit 0; }; c=$(cat /sys/fs/pstore/console-ramoops* 2>/dev/null | grep -ci "avc:"); echo "AVC_PSTORE_COUNT=$c"'
checks.description: Evidence: counts 'avc:' denials from previous boot if pstore is enabled.
checks.remediation: Investigate prior-boot AVC denials in /sys/fs/pstore/console-ramoops and update policy to prevent recurring issues.

checks.label: Android: live kernel log denials via /proc/kmsg (short sample)
checks.command: sh -c 'if [ -r /proc/kmsg ]; then (timeout 2 cat /proc/kmsg 2>/dev/null || true) | grep -i "avc:" | head -n 20; else echo NO_KMSG; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: samples kernel messages for 'avc:' (may require root; timeout avoids blocking).
checks.remediation: Use audit2allow to analyze /proc/kmsg AVC denials and generate policy modules for legitimate access.

checks.label: Linux: kernel log AVC count via journalctl (if available)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then c=$(journalctl -k 2>/dev/null | grep -ci "avc:" ); echo "AVC_JOURNALCTL_COUNT=$c"; else echo NO_JOURNALCTL; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: counts AVC denials in kernel journal (availability depends on system logging).
checks.remediation: Run 'journalctl -k | grep avc' to review denials. Use audit2allow to create policy fixes for valid access.

checks.label: Linux: audit.log AVC count (if audit log exists)
checks.command: sh -c 'if [ -r /var/log/audit/audit.log ]; then c=$(grep -ci "avc:" /var/log/audit/audit.log 2>/dev/null); echo "AVC_AUDITLOG_COUNT=$c"; else echo NO_AUDIT_LOG; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: counts AVC denials in auditd log if present.
checks.remediation: Review /var/log/audit/audit.log for AVC entries. Use audit2allow to generate targeted policy modules.

checks.label: Linux: ausearch recent AVC events (if ausearch exists)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v ausearch >/dev/null 2>&1; then ausearch -m avc -ts recent 2>/dev/null | head -n 40; else echo NO_AUSEARCH; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: shows recent AVC events via audit tooling (requires audit subsystem/logs).
checks.remediation: Install audit and policycoreutils-python-utils. Use 'ausearch -m avc | audit2allow' to diagnose and fix denials.

checks.label: Linux: auditd service active (systemd systems)
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then systemctl is-active auditd 2>/dev/null || true; else echo NO_SYSTEMCTL; fi'
checks.description: Evidence: checks auditd status where systemd is used.
checks.remediation: Enable auditd with 'systemctl enable --now auditd'. Install the audit package if not present.

checks.label: Bootloader SELinux Override Not Permissive
checks.command: sh -c 'v=$(getprop ro.boot.selinux 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$v" ] || [ "$v" = "enforcing" ]; then echo OK; else echo "OVERRIDE=$v"; fi'
checks.description: ro.boot.selinux is set by the bootloader and can override runtime enforcing. If set to 'permissive', device is globally permissive regardless of getenforce output. Empty or 'enforcing' = safe.
checks.remediation: Reflash the bootloader or update boot config to remove the permissive SELinux override. Lock the bootloader.

checks.label: SELinux Enforce File Not World-Writable
checks.command: sh -c 'if [ -e /sys/fs/selinux/enforce ]; then perms=$(ls -la /sys/fs/selinux/enforce 2>/dev/null | awk "{print \$1}"); echo "$perms" | grep -qE '^.{8}[^-]' && echo WRITABLE || echo OK; else echo NO_FILE; fi'
checks.description: If /sys/fs/selinux/enforce is world-writable, any process can disable SELinux without root. Should be read-only for non-root. WRITABLE = critical misconfiguration.
checks.remediation: Run 'chmod 644 /sys/fs/selinux/enforce' to restrict write access. Investigate how permissions were changed.

checks.label: No Individual Permissive Domains
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1; then out=$(semanage permissive -l 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$out" ] && echo CLEAN || echo "$out"; elif [ -r /sys/fs/selinux/policy ]; then # Android: check for permissive= in policy attributes via getprop out=$(getprop | grep -i permissive 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$out" ] && echo CLEAN || echo "$out"; else echo NO_TOOL; fi'
checks.description: A device can report global Enforcing mode while individual critical domains (e.g. untrusted_app, shell) are set permissive. semanage permissive -l lists them on Linux; getprop permissive hint on Android. NO_TOOL = tool not available, not a failure.
checks.remediation: Remove permissive domains with 'semanage permissive -d <domain>'. Ensure no domain is individually set to permissive.

checks.label: SELinux Policy Version
checks.command: cat /sys/fs/selinux/policyvers 2>/dev/null
checks.description: Reports the SELinux policy version loaded in the kernel. Modern Android (12+) ships with policy version 30 or higher. A markedly lower version suggests a downgraded or custom policy, often associated with rooted or modified devices.
checks.remediation: Lower than expected policy versions warrant investigation: check whether a custom kernel or sepolicy patch was applied, and reflash stock firmware if integrity is required.

checks.label: checkreqprot is 0 (kernel evaluates effective protection)
checks.command: sh -c 'out=$(cat /sys/fs/selinux/checkreqprot 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$out" ]; then echo NA; else echo "$out"; fi'
checks.description: /sys/fs/selinux/checkreqprot controls whether the kernel checks the requested (legacy, weaker, value 1) or effective (modern, value 0) protection on mmap and mprotect. Modern Android with kernel 5.x defaults to 0. NA means the sysfs entry has been removed in newer kernels (6.4+), which is also safe.
checks.remediation: Set the kernel default via SELINUX_CHECKREQPROT_VALUE=0 in the kernel config or via boot-time mount option. On Android this is a kernel-build decision; if you find 1 on a production device, investigate why the kernel was downgraded.
checks.why: checkreqprot=1 is a known bypass vector for W^X and exec-page exploits because the kernel only checks the protection the app asked for, not the protection it actually got after kernel mapping.
checks.risk_if_fail: Kernel evaluates a weaker protection than what is effective, undermining mprotect-based mitigations and enabling certain code-injection chains.

checks.label: MLS is enabled in the loaded policy (/sys/fs/selinux/mls = 1)
checks.command: sh -c 'out=$(cat /sys/fs/selinux/mls 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$out" ]; then echo NA; else echo "$out"; fi'
checks.description: /sys/fs/selinux/mls reports whether MLS (Multi-Level Security) is compiled into the loaded policy. MLS is what powers Android's per-app MCS category isolation, the boundary between any two installed apps on the same device. A value of 0 means MLS is off and the per-app sandbox no longer enforces category separation. NA on a non-Android Linux is acceptable.
checks.remediation: Build the kernel and SELinux policy with MLS support (CONFIG_SECURITY_SELINUX_MLS=y or equivalent for the policy compiler). On Android this is the AOSP default; finding 0 indicates a custom build that removed MLS.
checks.why: Without MLS, app data isolation between user apps relies only on UID-based separation, which is a weaker boundary that has historically been bypassed via shared UID grouping or sandbox escapes.
checks.risk_if_fail: Apps on the same device may be able to read each other's data when sandbox boundaries are bypassed.

checks.label: No per-domain permissive denials recorded in dmesg
checks.command: sh -c 'if command -v dmesg >/dev/null 2>&1; then c=$(dmesg 2>/dev/null | grep -ci "permissive=1"); echo "PERMISSIVE_AVC_COUNT=$c"; else echo NO_DMESG; fi'
checks.description: Even when getenforce reports Enforcing globally, individual domains can be marked permissive (typically via magiskpolicy or a sepolicy-inject patch). Each AVC denial for a permissive domain carries permissive=1 in dmesg. Any non-zero count indicates at least one domain is bypassing enforcement.
checks.remediation: Inspect the offending AVC denials: 'dmesg | grep permissive=1 | head -20'. The scontext field identifies the permissive domain. If you did not deliberately mark a domain permissive (e.g. for development), reflash to stock and audit for runtime SELinux tampering.
checks.why: Per-domain permissive is a stealthier attack than fully disabling SELinux: getenforce still reports Enforcing, the kernel cmdline check still passes, but specific domains (often relevant to an exploit) silently bypass policy.
checks.risk_if_fail: Targeted SELinux bypass for a specific attack chain, undetectable by the standard getenforce / ro.boot.selinux checks.

checks.label: No offensive policy-tampering tools present on disk
checks.command: sh -c 'found=""; for f in /data/local/tmp/sepolicy-inject /data/local/tmp/sepolicy_inject /data/local/tmp/sesearch /data/local/tmp/seinfo /data/local/tmp/setools /data/local/sepolicy-inject /sbin/sepolicy-inject /system/xbin/sepolicy-inject /system/bin/sepolicy-inject /data/local/tmp/magiskpolicy; do [ -e "$f" ] && found="$found $f"; done; if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo NONE; else echo "FOUND:$found"; fi'
checks.description: sepolicy-inject (from the setools fork), sesearch, seinfo (from setools-android), and magiskpolicy are not shipped on any stock Android device. Their presence in /data/local/tmp or other writable locations is a strong indicator that someone has been parsing or modifying the running SELinux policy. The 8ksec SELinux Internals blog walks through using exactly these tools to inject allow rules and bypass restrictions.
checks.remediation: Remove the listed binaries. Investigate how they were placed: ADB push by a developer, a malicious app extracting them from assets, or a leftover from a security-testing session. On a production device, none of these should ever exist.
checks.why: These tools have no legitimate purpose on a production device. Their presence demonstrates intent or active capability to modify SELinux policy at runtime.
checks.risk_if_fail: SELinux policy may have been (or may currently be being) modified to allow privileged operations that the original policy denies.

checks.label: Property Context Labelling Coverage
checks.command: F=$(ls /system/etc/selinux/*property_contexts* /vendor/etc/selinux/*property_contexts* /plat_property_contexts /vendor_property_contexts 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '); if [ -z "$F" ]; then echo NO_PROPERTY_CONTEXTS; else T=$(cat $F 2>/dev/null | grep -cvE '^\s*(#|$)'); D=$(cat $F 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'default_prop'); echo "files=$(echo $F | wc -w) entries=$T default_prop_entries=$D"; fi
checks.description: Counts the SELinux property context definitions and how many map to default_prop. Android's property service enforces write access by SELinux label, so a property left at the catch-all default_prop label is writable by any domain the policy grants default_prop write to, which is usually broader than intended. Vendor-added properties that control privileged behaviour and are left unlabelled are a recurring source of privilege escalation through init service triggers. Reported as an inventory because a nonzero default_prop count is normal and only a policy reviewer can judge which entries matter.
checks.remediation: Give every vendor property an explicit SELinux type rather than leaving it at default_prop, and confirm no property that triggers an init action is writable by an untrusted domain.
